import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/nls_raw.csv')

# Select the relevant columns
gender_column = 'Sex of respondent, 1979'
degree_completion_column = 'Highest grade completed, 1979'

# Filter out rows with missing values
df_filtered = df[[gender_column, degree_completion_column]].dropna()

# Convert gender to categorical labels
df_filtered[gender_column] = df_filtered[gender_column].map({1: 'Male', 2: 'Female'})

# Display the first few rows of the filtered dataset
df_filtered.head()

# Create a boxplot to visualize the relationship between gender and degree completion rates
sns.boxplot(x=gender_column, y=degree_completion_column, data=df_filtered)
plt.title('Relationship between Gender and Degree Completion Rates')
plt.xlabel('Gender')
plt.ylabel('Highest Grade Completed')
plt.show()

# Perform a t-test to determine if there is a statistically significant difference in degree completion rates between genders
male_degrees = df_filtered[df_filtered[gender_column] == 'Male'][degree_completion_column]
female_degrees = df_filtered[df_filtered[gender_column] == 'Female'][degree_completion_column]

t_statistic, p_value = ttest_ind(male_degrees, female_degrees)
t_statistic, p_value
